intro.text: This entry describes spermatogenic failure 104 (SPGF104), a form of male infertility. I do not reliably remember which gene and which primary reports define this entry, so no causal gene is given here.

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure 104 (SPGF104) is a form of male infertility.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract describes a homozygous CCDC9 variant in a patient with severe asthenozoospermia, but it never mentions SPGF104 or any numbered spermatogenic failure entry. Only the abstract was supplied.

paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure 104 (SPGF104) is one of a numbered series of genetically defined forms of male infertility caused by defective sperm production or sperm function. The specific gene, the sperm phenotype (for example, azoospermia versus a sperm morphology or motility defect), and the reports that established this entry are not recalled here with enough confidence to state them.

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure 104 (SPGF104) is one of a numbered series of genetically defined forms of male infertility.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention the numbered SPGF series or SPGF104.

checks.claim: The numbered spermatogenic failure (SPGF) forms of male infertility, including SPGF104, are caused by defective sperm production or sperm function.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss the SPGF series or what causes it. It covers only CCDC9 in severe asthenozoospermia.

paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure is genetically heterogeneous. Many numbered SPGF entries are each caused by mutation in a different gene.

checks.evidence_quote: There are likely to be hundreds of monogenic forms of human male infertility.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports genetic heterogeneity of male infertility in general (hundreds of monogenic forms; causal variants in five different genes), but it does not use the term spermatogenic failure.

checks.claim: Many numbered spermatogenic failure (SPGF) entries are each caused by mutation in a different gene.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention numbered SPGF entries or their causal genes.
